spec_match.rationale: Composes the API with the exact workload it exists to diagnose: a genuine RTCPeerConnection loopback (offer/answer, ICE, data channel, getStats) bracketed by startDiagnosticLogging({ metadata }) / finishDiagnosticLogging on success and cancelDiagnosticLogging on failure — the keep-vs-discard decision the spec's lifecycle is for; the silent-resolve section demonstrates the spec's 'no guarantees of success' privacy model with real double-start calls, never a simulation.

interactive.rationale: The primary button runs a real call in ANY modern browser — connection-state timeline, ICE candidate log, measured data-channel round trip, and a live getStats readout (selected candidate pair, transport bytes) — so unlike the other concepts this page has a fully real primary interaction even without the flag; the capture bracket engages only when the API is exposed and the page states which of the two actually happened.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card promises the wrapped real call plus the silent-resolve privacy demonstration; the page delivers both.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers capture-unavailable (call still runs, wrap honestly skipped), call-failure (10s ICE timeout → error status + cancelDiagnosticLogging discard path), missing RTCPeerConnection entirely, and the second-start silent-resolve edge; the double-start button also records honestly if an implementation rejects instead of silently resolving.

references.rationale: See-also cites chromestatus.com/feature/5091582546149376; the capture note links the origin-trial registration; the spec's privacy-model language is quoted and attributable via the feature index's spec link.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's binding-agnostic assertions cover the surfaces this page calls (start/finish/cancel through either binding, metadata validation); the loopback workload itself is baseline WebRTC and deliberately not asserted as a diagnostic-logging contract.

runtime_evidence.rationale: End-to-end CDP verification on headless Chromium 141 with ?autorun=1: connectionState reached 'connected', ICE pair 'host ↔ host', data-channel round trip 0.70 ms, transport bytes 1171/1169, timeline populated, capture wrap honestly reported as skipped ('not started — API not exposed'), zero console errors; post-interaction screenshots read at desktop and 360×740. The bracketed (bound) variant and the silent-resolve button need a flag-capable Chrome 151+ — recorded as an open question, and the double-start button is honestly disabled with its reason when unbound.

telemetry_health.rationale: Branch asserts: rtc-loopback-connected (can fail on timeout, with the error recorded), rtc-capture-wrap-started / rtc-capture-wrap-unavailable (the latter observed firing in the harness), rtc-silent-resolve-observed, and rtc-loopback-no-webrtc; ICE candidate races are caught so no unhandled rejections reach the collector.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; stats table header inverts background+color; status colours are accent variables on light backgrounds; timeline log reuses the family's log styling.

accessibility.rationale: role=status aria-live status line, role=log aria-live timeline, aria-live session readout and silent-resolve output, semantic stats table with caption + th scope, native buttons; the disabled double-start button's reason is stated in the adjacent visible live region rather than hidden.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Feature harness desktop OK / mobile OK; this concept measured 0px horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3 with zero console errors during a full autorun call, and the 360px post-interaction screenshot was read: timeline, stats table, and notes all legible with wrapped tokens.

openQuestions.title: Run the captured (bound) variant and the silent-resolve demonstration on Chrome 151+ behind the flag
openQuestions.detail: In the harness (Chromium 141, API absent) the loopback call itself verified end-to-end but the capture bracket ran its honest skip branch and the double-start button stayed disabled. On Chrome 151+ with --enable-blink-features=RTCDiagnosticLogging, run the full bracketed call (session UUID appears, finish resolves) and the ×2 start + cancel sequence, and confirm whether Chromium resolves the second start with a distinct UUID as the spec describes.

openQuestions.title: Consider surfacing candidate-pair currentRoundTripTime alongside the data-channel RTT
openQuestions.detail: getStats exposes currentRoundTripTime on the succeeded candidate-pair; showing it next to the app-level data-channel round trip would let visitors compare transport-level and app-level latency in the same readout. Additive polish only.

guidanceConsulted.query: status live region announcements for async API call results
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce multi-step async progress through live regions and keep visual timelines mirrored in accessible text.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the call timeline is a role=log live region receiving each step as text; status, session, and silent-resolve outputs are aria-live; the stats readout is a semantic captioned table rather than a visual-only panel.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP autorun 2026-08-16: timeline text observed accumulating; zero console errors

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive stats table and log panel without horizontal overflow on narrow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wrap long tokens inside cells and let control rows wrap instead of fixing widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: overflow-wrap:anywhere on table cells and code, flex-wrap control rows, scrollable log capped in height; measured 0px overflow at 360×740 mid-call.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: mobile-check CDP run 2026-08-16: scrollWidth − innerWidth = 0 at 360px with autorun

summary: New concept for v151 (not in the v150 predecessor), filling the portfolio's advanced-composition angle: a real RTCPeerConnection loopback call — verified connecting end-to-end in the harness with live stats — bracketed by the diagnostic-logging lifecycle, plus an interactive demonstration of the spec's silent-resolve privacy model. Gives every visitor a genuinely working primary interaction even where the API is absent, while keeping the capture wrap strictly honest about whether it engaged.
